newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bund futures lower, but dull trade expected.
newsitem.headline: Bund futures lower, but dull trade expected.

text.p: Bund futures were lower in early trade as weak Treasuries and a technical rebound off recent highs weighed on prices.
Traders said they expected dull trade on the day with nothing but the Franco-German summit in Lyon expected to offer any reason to take new positions.
At 0930 GMT, the DTB June Bund futures contract was down 13 basis points at 101.71, after trading in range between 101.62 to 101.89.
The recently volatile yield curve, meanwhile, was little changed between two and 10-years at around 203 basis points.

At the Franco-German summit in Lyon, Finance Minister Theo Waigel said that Germany was still in a good position to meet the three percent Maastricht deficit target and that Germany and France have a good chance of achieving 2.5 percent economic growth in 1997.
Traders said they expected exactly that sort of statement from the meeting and doubted that officials there will offer any market-moving comments about EMU.
T-notes outperformed Bunds, pushing the spread to 101 basis ponits from 104 basis points at the previous close.
Analysts see support for the contract around 101.50, a congestive chart point, and that futures should hold around that level for lack of any concrete news.
The Federal Statistics Office said the number of insolvencies in Germany reached a record high in 1996 for the fourth year in a row, climbing 9.3 percent to 31,471.
The data, however, had little impact on Bund prices.
